messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page triggered (PD#RD-9421) — Region: us-west-2 (multiple AZs reporting high 5xx rate). Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

oncall-pagerduty: PagerDuty delivered to alex kim (primary).

alex kim: acked in PD. I can take initial triage. Seeing spike in 504/502 from inference-proxy in us-west-2-a and us-west-2-b.

maya singh: I’m looking at LB health -> a bunch of backend hosts are failing healthchecks, likely kernel OOMs on gpu-1 nodes. Not all AZs but concentrated.

paul r.: confirming — Cloud metrics show pod restarts on dedicated-gpu-pool-usw2. CPU stable but GPU mem pressure high. Possible runaway batch sizes or a regressed model load.

alex kim: Opening the mitigation playbook: ops-runbook-bot link: https://runbook.redwood.internal/incidents/auto-failover.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook steps: 1) Evacuate unhealthy hosts 2) Activate cross-region fallback -> us-east-1 3) Temporarily route traffic to model-compact variant. Use commands below.

gina l.: quick note — customers on dedicated contracts in EU might be affected if we fail over; need to limit cross-region for those tenants. Adding sticky-exempt list now.

alex kim: Step 1: cordon and drain unhealthy nodes in us-west-2-a:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Draining more affected nodes.

maya singh: Killed a runaway GRPC worker process on gpu-node-51; memory freed. Restarting the inference-daemon with smaller batch concurrency:
```
kubectl set env ds/inference-daemon BATCH_CONCURRENCY=4 -n serving
```

paul r.: While drains happen, enabling fallback routing in the router:
```
routerctl set-route --region us-west-2 --fallback-region us-east-1 --model-policy model:compact,model:latency-50
```
This will send new sessions to compact variant in us-east-1.

alex kim: Paging escalation: if not stable in 10m, escalate to SRE lead @gina l.

oncall-pagerduty: alex kim acknowledged, escalation timer set (10m).

maya singh: Health checks improving on some nodes after restart. 5xx rate down from 8% -> 2.5% but still over threshold for a few routes (/v1/chat/completions).

gina l.: I’m in. Checking autoscale — dedicated pool autoscaler didn't trigger because of a bad metric tag. Overriding to force scale +2 GPUs in usw2:
```
infractl scale --pool dedicated-gpu-usw2 --delta +2
```

paul r.: Forced scale accepted, new instances provisioning. ETA ~3m. Also rolling back a recent agent change that increased prefetch window on serving runtime.

alex kim: Customer impact: degraded latency and 5xxs for customers in us-west-2. Noticing a spike of error reports from a handful of enterprise tenants using pinned dedicated clusters. Notifying CS.

gina l.: Re: enterprise tenants — adding sticky exemption for clusters with 'no-failover' tag. Running command:
```
routerctl exempt-add --tag no-failover --region wsz
```

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: update incident channel with estimated customer impact and mitigation steps.

maya singh: Metrics now: 5xx=0.8% cluster-wide, latency P95 within SLO for compact variant. Original variant still recovering in us-west-2.

alex kim: Good. Cancel escalation timer. oncall-pagerduty: resolve PD alert? Wait for stability window 15m.

oncall-pagerduty: Escalation timer cancelled. PD alert remains active until manual resolve.

paul r.: Follow-up: root cause appears to be increased KV cache growth on a new model loader that wasn't evicting properly -> OOM cascade on some GPU nodes. Rolling back the model loader change and patching eviction policy.

gina l.: Creating a hotfix PR for eviction and a configuration guard to prevent >BATCH_CONCURRENCY=8 on these pools.

alex kim: Handing off active monitoring to @maya for 2hr post-incident watch. Handoff note: keep fallback routing active for now, but begin re-routing back once all hosts report healthy and 5xx < 0.2% for 15m.

maya singh: Taking it. I'll post a status update every 15m.

ops-runbook-bot: Status snapshot (automated):
- Region: us-west-2
- Status: degraded -> recovering
- Active mitigations: node drains, scale +2, model rollback, fallback routing to us-east-1, sticky exemptions for no-failover clusters
- Customer impact: targeted degraded responses for ~6 enterprise tenants in usw2, broader transient latency increase for ~300 dev accounts

alex kim: Notifying CS + success team with summary and mitigation steps. Drafting message for affected customers.

gina l.: PD incident updated with root cause summary and action items (hotfix, config guard, audit of model loader changes).

paul r.: After scale completes, we're seeing baseline restored. I’m beginning to disable fallback routing and gradually shift traffic back to model-original variant.

alex kim: All routes back to normal. 5xx < 0.1% for 30m. No active escalations.

incident-bot: Incident (PD#RD-9421) marked RESOLVED by alex kim. Duration: ~52 minutes.

alex kim: Summary: OOM cascade caused by model loader eviction bug -> node restarts -> increased 5xx. Mitigations: drained nodes, scaled pool, rolled back model loader change, enabled cross-region fallback and sticky exemptions for protected tenants. Postmortem + timeline assigned to maya singh, due EOD+2.

maya singh: I'll own the postmortem. Will include perf regression detection rule and a runtime guard.

gina l.: Adding action: update autoscaler metric tags and add PD playbook test to our chaos runbook.

paul r.: Thanks all. Closing monitoring loop but keeping watch for next 2h. :thumbsup:

alex kim: Great work team.
